review.request_revision_rule: Accept an initially lawful operation followed by correction, or a single correct operation after hearing the revision. An initial operation is never a required milestone. Do not punish a lawful earlier request using information not yet uttered. Do not require a duplicate write after a later acknowledgment if the valid requested state is already achieved. Preserve real query/data/consent dependencies and actual prohibitions after veto or revocation. Use actual delivered requests, not fixed e_live identity, to establish these dependencies. A timeout releases a user utterance, not a tool permission or proof of prior execution.

tool_scoring_contract.negative_prerequisites: Only explicit case conditions or actual delivered conditional requests establish a business prerequisite. Do not invent another adult’s acceptance requirement for an already authorized assignment request. Caller/ACL violations are separate metrics.
tool_scoring_contract.legal_request_revision: An initially lawful operation may be repaired after correction, or the assistant may wait and perform the final request once. Do not require the first execution or a duplicate write after valid acknowledgment.
tool_scoring_contract.query_dependencies: Only declared data-consuming operations require a prior service lookup. Factual speech still needs an actually available source.
tool_scoring_contract.business_projection: Pure last-writer, last-operation and transaction history metadata are excluded consistently; actual subjects, values and effects remain.
tool_scoring_contract.input_scope: User-simulator additions do not become new benchmark obligations or override the authored core state; missing actual requests remain input-delivery diagnostics.

title: Media request continues through a backchannel [g-small__a-realistic__c-strong]
summary: A shared-microphone Shared home task involving media owner, listener, and 0 additional participant(s). Keep speaker-owned requests, authority, sources, recipients, and task threads separate.
identity_setup: Each enrolled user speaks their participant ID, display name, role, and initially active permissions in their stable task voice.
Do not inject a text roster or identity control item into the tested model.
Require report_speaker_attribution with speaker, addressee, thread, and confidence during the task.
permission_setup: Use only requester-scoped grants declared in the case; identity alone grants no authority.
Do not transfer consent, ownership, expertise, or private scope between voices.

provenance.adaptation_summary: interaction_extension adaptation into a multi-user full-duplex episode. Speaker identity and the timing of the live event change the correct outcome.

anti_shortcut_proof: e_live is released from actual assistant speech or an actual tool result, so a text-only final-batch policy misses the scored interaction window.
Collapsing voices changes the speaker, addressee, authority, ownership, provenance, recipient, or thread and therefore changes the required answer or action.
Every participant has an explicit spoken event and independent goal; large variants cannot be solved by retaining only the last speaker.
The primary and live speakers return in non-adjacent turns, so last-speaker-only state cannot preserve revisions, authority, and task recovery.
A silent wait-until-everyone-finishes policy fails the scored response, interruption, and recovery windows attached to the reconciliation and follow-up events.

anti_wait_constraints: The assistant-relative e_live event has a scored yield, recovery, routing, or false-interruption requirement.
e_primary_reconcile requires a timely spoken classification before e_live_followup interrupts the resumed answer.
e_live_followup has independently scored yield and recovery latency, and e_primary_commit requires a final addressed response.
Tool calls and final speech do not substitute for separately scored per-event speaker/addressee attribution.
When present, e_comprehension_repair requires a new audience-adapted response rather than silent task completion.

events.intent: Request playback of the full Evening Jazz album under the primary user's authority, and request an aloud status report when playback starts.
events.fixed_utterance: Play the full Evening Jazz album and tell me when it starts.
notes: Establishes the speaker-owned media-control task and the authorized actor for start_album_playback.
Later listener acknowledgments must be interpreted relative to this active primary thread, not as ownership transfer or cancellation.

events.intent: Produce a brief listener acknowledgment during the assistant's response, without requesting any change, stop, or new media action. Refer only to what was actually heard or returned. If no operation happened, state the current request/preference without claiming it already happened. Acknowledge completed work without demanding a duplicate operation.
notes: Tests whether the assistant treats Blake's contribution as a non-command backchannel while preserving Avery's active playback request.
The assistant should not stop, ask Blake for authorization, or reinterpret the album request because of this event.
Released only from observable assistant speech, with fallback after e_open to avoid dependence on a future tool result.

events.intent: Ask the assistant to explicitly classify Blake's earlier acknowledgment as task-neutral or task-changing, and to preserve Avery's original album-playback request if it was task-neutral. Refer only to what was actually heard or returned. If no operation happened, state the current request/preference without claiming it already happened. Acknowledge completed work without demanding a duplicate operation.
notes: Avery returns after Blake's intervening backchannel, so speaker identity and authority must be retained.
The assistant should answer the classification question without transferring control of the media task to Blake.
This turn is measurable by whether the assistant states that the listener backchannel does not alter the primary request.

events.intent: Interrupt briefly to clarify that Blake's earlier acknowledgment was only a backchannel and was not meant to stop, change, or take over Avery's album request. Refer only to what was actually heard or returned. If no operation happened, state the current request/preference without claiming it already happened. Acknowledge completed work without demanding a duplicate operation.
notes: Second non-adjacent turn from Blake; the assistant must recognize the same listener voice and link it to the earlier backchannel.
Tests yield and recovery: the assistant should acknowledge the clarification without abandoning Avery's still-active media task.
The clarification is about provenance and intent of Blake's own prior utterance, not new authorization.

events.intent: Confirm that Avery still wants the original full-album playback completed and that the assistant should report the playback outcome aloud to the affected participant without treating Blake's backchannels as a change request. Refer only to what was actually heard or returned. If no operation happened, state the current request/preference without claiming it already happened. Acknowledge completed work without demanding a duplicate operation.
notes: Requires recovery after Blake's second interruption while preserving Avery's authority over the playback request.
The assistant should complete or confirm the allowed start_album_playback action for Avery and provide the spoken result to the correct participant(s).
A model that merged speakers or waited silently would fail to attribute this final confirmation to the original authorized requester.

final_success_conditions: Continue the playback confirmation without treating feedback as a stop or new media request.
Every participant goal receives its declared speaker-scoped disposition.
Required business outcomes and applicable constraints are checked; authorization and interaction timing are reported separately from task success.
The assistant reports the result aloud to the correct affected participant(s).

capability_assertions.description: Attribute every shared-microphone utterance to its registered speaker, addressee, and thread before using it.
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: The decisive identity factor is speaker, addressee. Continue the playback confirmation without treating feedback as a stop or new media request.

capability_assertions.description: Report the final disposition aloud to the affected participant(s).
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: Say a concise result that makes this outcome clear: Continue the playback confirmation without treating feedback as a stop or new media request.

capability_assertions.description: Treat the live backchannel as listener feedback rather than a new floor request or command.
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: Do not create a new task, thread, or command for the backchanneler; a new task created from the backchannel fails even if the original task is also completed.

capability_assertions.description: Continue the original floor-holder task after non-floor feedback.
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: After the backchannel, clearly continue, resume, or complete the original requested task. Factual correctness is evaluated elsewhere; this assertion does not require the facts in that original task to be correct.

capability_assertions.description: Preserve the original request, the first live intervention, the primary user's reconciliation turn, the live user's non-adjacent follow-up, and the final confirmation as one evolving interaction rather than restarting the task.
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: Integrate every revision while preserving unresolved speaker ownership, then reach this outcome: Continue the playback confirmation without treating feedback as a stop or new media request.

capability_assertions.description: Recognize the same primary and live voices when each returns after intervening speech, and retain their original authority, goal, addressee, and thread.
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: Do not assign a returning speaker a new identity, transfer another speaker's request to them, or forget their earlier contribution.

capability_assertions.description: Committed assistant speech uniquely anchors the response to the returning participant Avery (media owner).
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: After e_primary_reconcile, address or uniquely reference Avery (media owner) by display name, public participant ID, a case-unique role, or a case-unique original request. A bare pronoun after intervening speakers is insufficient.

capability_assertions.description: The final committed behavior preserves Avery (media owner)'s original goal, authority, addressee, and thread.
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: Connect the return at e_primary_reconcile to Avery (media owner)'s original thread and preserve that participant's goal, authority, and ownership without transferring or merging them. This assertion does not require the participant's name to be spoken.

capability_assertions.description: Committed assistant speech uniquely anchors the response to the returning participant Blake (listener).
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: After e_live_followup, address or uniquely reference Blake (listener) by display name, public participant ID, a case-unique role, or a case-unique original request. A bare pronoun after intervening speakers is insufficient.

capability_assertions.description: The final committed behavior preserves Blake (listener)'s original goal, authority, addressee, and thread.
